Check if the diagnostic messages start with a timestamp.

## Signature

```typescript
get timestamp(): boolean;
```

## Remarks

It is the value of the `timestamp` option of the constructor, and it cannot be changed after the logger is created.

If it is true, the messages of the methods that have a prefix (`error()`<!-- -->, `warn()`<!-- -->, `debug()`<!-- -->, and `trace()`<!-- -->) start with the local time, without the time zone, as `YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss.SSS`<!-- -->, and the prefix is replaced by the kind of the message in square brackets:

```text
2026-11-11 23:32:31.358 [warning] the file is missing
```
The stamp is tied to the method, not to the prefix that is written, and is only on the first line of a message. The rules are in the section "Timestamps" of the User's Guide.

<ul> <li>added in v7.0.0</li> </ul>
